source: Published patent applications reviewed as directional evidence of competitor technical and workflow investment
methodology: Records are filtered by publication date because that is when an application becomes publicly observable. Analyst implications describe possible roadmap relevance and do not assert product availability, claim scope, validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Modeled reference chromatograms for instrument qualification
insights.signal: The application describes synthesizing a reference chromatogram from statistical, simulation, or artificial-intelligence models and comparing it with a measured chromatogram to evaluate chromatography operating conditions.
insights.roadmapImplication: Compare how Waters could support configuration-aware qualification, system-suitability review, and method transfer without turning modeled chromatograms into unsupported performance claims.
insights.watchNext: Agilent software releases using modeled reference chromatograms, validation material for regulated laboratories, and evidence that the approach reduces qualification effort.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The pending filing describes possible modeling and evaluation techniques. It does not establish implementation, regulatory acceptance, customer adoption, model accuracy, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Valve-and-cartridge architecture for configurable two-dimensional chromatography
insights.officialTitle: Systems and methods for two-dimensional chromatography
insights.signal: The application describes first- and second-dimension separation columns connected through switching and sampling valves, with fraction-capture devices for heart-cut workflows and SFC or HPLC combinations.
insights.roadmapImplication: Benchmark Waters multidimensional-LC fluidics, fraction handling, retrofit paths, and downstream detector integration against the configurable valve and cartridge architecture described here.
insights.watchNext: National-stage claims, commercial valve modules, 2D-LC application notes, and evidence connecting the architecture to reproducibility, recovery, or workflow simplicity.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The pending international application describes possible system configurations. It does not establish commercial implementation, final claim scope, comparative performance, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Mixed-mode polymeric stationary phase for protein and nucleic-acid separations
insights.officialTitle: Polymeric ion exchange-reversed phase-mixed-mode chromatography stationary phase for analysis of proteins and nucleic acids
insights.signal: The application describes weakly charged porous polymer particles that combine hydrophobic and ionic retention modes for proteins and nucleic acids, including mass-spectrometry-compatible mobile phases.
insights.roadmapImplication: Compare Waters biopolymer column selectivity, MS-compatible buffer choices, ion-pair-free methods, and oligonucleotide or protein workflow coverage against this mixed-mode concept.
insights.watchNext: National-stage prosecution, Dionex or Thermo Fisher column launches, application data for oligonucleotides and proteins, and method robustness across sample classes.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The pending application describes media compositions and separation methods. It does not establish a shipping column, final claim scope, comparative selectivity, lifetime, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Dual-energy MS1 scans for identifying intact precursor peaks
insights.officialTitle: Methods and apparatus for mass spectrometry
insights.signal: The granted patent compares MS1 scans acquired with different ion-transport energies to distinguish precursor peaks from transport-induced fragments and support subsequent DIA interpretation.
insights.roadmapImplication: Test whether Waters LC-MS acquisition and review workflows expose precursor-confidence evidence with comparable clarity while managing the sensitivity and cycle-time trade-offs of softer ion transport.
insights.watchNext: Thermo Fisher method templates, software controls exposing paired MS1 logic, proteomics application notes, and comparative evidence for precursor assignment and duty cycle.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2025, but the record does not establish implementation in a current instrument, product-level performance, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.assignee: Thermo Fisher Scientific Bremen GmbH; California Institute of Technology
insights.title: Parallel microscale electrostatic ion-trap arrays
insights.signal: The granted patent describes arrays of sub-10-millimeter electrostatic traps for parallel ion analysis, including image-current detection and optional in-trap fragmentation for MS/MS or MSn operation.
insights.roadmapImplication: Monitor whether parallel microscale analyzers change expected LC-MS throughput, ion utilization, or instrument footprint, and compare those possibilities with Waters analyzer-development priorities.
insights.watchNext: Continuation activity, prototype disclosures, instrument integrations, and measured evidence for resolving power, ion utilization, parallel throughput, and manufacturability.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2025, but it does not establish a commercial analyzer, scalable manufacturing, comparative performance, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Bayesian optimization of LC-MS source and separation parameters
insights.officialTitle: Mass spectrometer and program for mass spectrometer
insights.signal: The granted patent applies Bayesian optimization to LC-MS device parameters, including source conditions and possible LC flow, temperature, and solvent settings, then creates a method file from the selected result.
insights.roadmapImplication: Compare Waters method-development automation, parameter transparency, experiment count, and auditability with a workflow that jointly optimizes ionization and LC separation conditions.
insights.watchNext: Shimadzu software features exposing Bayesian optimization, regulated-workflow validation, application notes, and user evidence on time saved versus manual optimization.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2024, but it does not establish current product implementation, optimization quality across assays, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Internal-standard correction for chromatographic MS quantitation
insights.officialTitle: Chromatograph mass spectrometry data processing device and program
insights.signal: The application describes correcting target and stable-isotope internal-standard peak intensities with calibration, real, and correction samples to improve chromatographic mass-spectrometry quantitation.
insights.roadmapImplication: Assess whether Waters quantitative workflows make interference correction, calibration provenance, and matrix-effect handling equally explicit for LC-MS users and regulated reviewers.
insights.watchNext: National-stage claims, LabSolutions releases, supported analyzer types, validation studies, and customer evidence showing when correction materially changes quantitative results.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The English text is based on an international filing that includes translated material. The pending record does not establish final claims, implementation, comparative accuracy, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: DIA component detection and composition estimation for LC-MS
insights.officialTitle: Chromatograph mass spectrometry data processing method, chromatograph mass spectrometer, and chromatograph mass spectrometry data processing program
insights.signal: The granted patent processes retention-time, mass-to-charge, and intensity data from DIA MS/MS to detect compounds and partial structures, narrow candidates with prior information, and estimate composition.
insights.roadmapImplication: Compare Waters DIA interpretation for component detection, candidate narrowing, composition estimation, provenance, and analyst workload against the workflow described in this family.
insights.watchNext: Shimadzu software releases using the patented sequence, application examples, supported LC-MS platforms, and comparative evidence on identification quality and review effort.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2025, but it does not establish implementation in current software, comparative identification accuracy, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Well-plate-aware spectral matrix generation for high-throughput MS
insights.signal: The application describes a mass spectrometer and computing device that detect well-plate rows in sequential spectral data and generate a matrix mapping each row of wells to corresponding spectra.
insights.roadmapImplication: Evaluate how Waters connects plate identity, sampling order, spectral provenance, and exception handling in high-throughput workflows where automation errors can compromise an entire batch.
insights.watchNext: SCIEX automation releases, plate-handling integrations, supported sampling interfaces, and user evidence on throughput, traceability, and recovery from skipped or failed wells.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The pending application describes a data-organization workflow. It does not establish commercial implementation, sample throughput, error rates, final claim scope, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Non-contact open-port sampling into an LC-MS analysis circuit
insights.officialTitle: Non-contact sampler with an open-port interface for liquid chromatography systems
insights.signal: The granted patent describes ejecting droplets into an open-port interface, moving them through a sample-transfer chamber, switching that chamber into an LC circuit, separating them on a column, and analyzing the eluent.
insights.roadmapImplication: Compare Waters autosampling, carryover control, well-plate throughput, valve architecture, and LC-MS integration with a non-contact open-port workflow that decouples sample receipt from analysis.
insights.watchNext: SCIEX or partner products using the architecture, application data for high-throughput assays, and measured carryover, recovery, injection precision, and cycle time.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2026, but it does not establish current product implementation, comparative sampling performance, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Bubble-segmented sample isolation in open-port transport liquid
insights.officialTitle: Bubble based sample isolation in a transport liquid
insights.signal: The granted patent describes using atmospheric bubbles in open-port-interface transport liquid to mark or isolate introduced samples while monitoring bubble generation around sample receipt.
insights.roadmapImplication: Assess whether Waters high-throughput sample transport needs equivalent sample-boundary detection, contamination controls, and fault recovery when discrete droplets move through a continuous liquid stream.
insights.watchNext: Commercial open-port implementations, control-software behavior, supported sample matrices, and measured evidence for sample isolation, carryover, recovery, and failure detection.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2026, but the record does not establish a shipping workflow, comparative carryover or recovery, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: High-flow flushing and delivery for open-port MS sampling probes
insights.officialTitle: High flowrate flushing for open port sampling probe
insights.signal: The granted patent describes closing an open-port sampling probe and increasing flow for sample delivery or flushing, including cleaning lines, clearing bubbles or clogs, and changing capture fluids.
insights.roadmapImplication: Compare Waters sampling-path wash strategies, clog recovery, viscous-solvent handling, and time-to-result with the open-versus-closed flow modes described in this patent.
insights.watchNext: Product implementations, automated wash methods, supported solvent ranges, and measured evidence for carryover, clog recovery, transport time, and consumable lifetime.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2026, but it does not establish commercial implementation, comparative maintenance outcomes, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.assignee: PerkinElmer Health Sciences Canada Inc; PerkinElmer US LLC
insights.title: Compact ion-beam deflectors for mass-spectrometry systems
insights.officialTitle: Deflectors for ion beams and mass spectrometry systems comprising the same
insights.signal: The application describes ion-beam deflectors and mass-spectrometry systems using them, with electrode structures intended to steer ions between source, guide, analyzer, or detector regions.
insights.roadmapImplication: Track whether compact ion-steering architectures affect PerkinElmer mass-spectrometer footprint, ion transmission, or serviceability, and compare those possibilities with Waters analyzer packaging.
insights.watchNext: European prosecution, national grants, related instrument disclosures, and measured evidence for transmission, resolution, contamination control, and manufacturability.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The pending European application describes possible ion-optics configurations. It does not establish implementation, final claim scope, comparative performance, validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Voltage-controlled cone-and-lens interface for ion transmission
insights.officialTitle: ION interfaces and systems and methods using them
insights.signal: The granted patent describes ion interfaces using multiple voltage-controlled elements, including cone and cylindrical-lens arrangements, to focus ions and manage transmission into downstream mass-spectrometer components.
insights.roadmapImplication: Compare Waters atmospheric-interface architecture, background control, transmission stability, cleaning access, and real-time voltage control with the multistage interface described here.
insights.watchNext: PerkinElmer instrument documentation, service materials, application evidence, and measured comparisons of sensitivity, background, robustness, and maintenance frequency.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The United States patent was granted in 2024, but it does not establish use in a current product, LC coupling, comparative sensitivity, claim validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Silicon-coated ion-source flow path for mass spectrometry
insights.signal: The published application describes an ion-source flow path with a silicon or silicon-hydride coating and a hydrogen carrier-gas method for ionizing and analyzing a sample by mass.
insights.roadmapImplication: Use this family as a prompt to compare source-path inertness, contamination control, maintenance burden, and analytical robustness across relevant Waters and Agilent MS workflows.
insights.watchNext: Implementation in commercial Agilent ion sources, application notes that connect the coating to reduced adsorption or maintenance, and controlled comparative evidence on sensitivity and uptime.
insights.evidenceBoundary: This family was granted in the United Kingdom in 2026, but the record does not establish implementation in a current product, LC-MS applicability, commercial performance, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: HPLC/MS monitoring of lipid stability in mRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticles
insights.officialTitle: High-performance liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry (HPLC/MS)-based apparatus and method for monitoring of lipid stability in messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) encapsulated lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) under different storage conditions
insights.signal: The published application describes an HPLC/MS apparatus and method for identifying and measuring lipid components in mRNA-loaded LNPs across storage and formulation conditions, including lyophilized and non-lyophilized samples.
insights.roadmapImplication: Evaluate whether Next Gen LC needs an LNP stability workflow package that connects separation, accurate-mass confirmation, calibration, sample preparation, and formulation-study reporting.
insights.watchNext: National-stage claims, an Agilent application note or launch using the workflow, and customer evidence that LNP stability monitoring is a buying criterion rather than a specialist method.
insights.evidenceBoundary: A pending application indicates an attempted area of protection. It does not establish granted claim scope, commercial availability, performance superiority, or customer adoption.

insights.title: Collision-cross-section-guided precursor selection for DDA mass spectrometry
insights.signal: The published application uses a collision-cross-section indicator to select or order DDA precursor targets and may adapt fragmentation energy or method, with explicit relevance to modified or cross-linked peptides and proteins.
insights.roadmapImplication: Pressure-test whether Waters acquisition workflows make precursor prioritization and fragmentation decisions equally transparent, reproducible, and useful for complex biopharma characterization.
insights.watchNext: Continuation filings, implementation in Orbitrap or multi-reflection TOF workflows, software-release notes, and comparative evidence on identification depth, duty cycle, and reproducibility.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The application describes proposed methods and possible analyzer implementations. It does not prove that a current Thermo Fisher product uses the claims or delivers a measured customer outcome.

insights.title: Peak tracking across liquid-chromatography conditions using molecular-weight correspondence
insights.signal: The application describes matching chromatographic peaks across different analysis conditions by calculating molecular weights from mass-to-charge data, reducing reliance on an unchanged mass-spectrum pattern during method development.
insights.roadmapImplication: Treat cross-condition peak correspondence as a workflow requirement for method scouting: assess whether Waters can shorten review time while preserving traceability when retention and spectral patterns shift.
insights.watchNext: US-family prosecution, software or method-development releases, supported detector combinations, and user evidence on reduced manual peak reconciliation.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The English abstract is a machine translation of a pending Japanese application. No claim is made about final scope, implementation quality, or availability in a Shimadzu product.

insights.title: Lower-complexity retention-time alignment for separation-coupled mass spectrometry
insights.officialTitle: Reducing data complexity for subsequent RT alignment
insights.signal: The application divides retention-time and mass-spectral data into m/z sub-ranges and independently aligns chromatographic peaks within those subsets to reduce data complexity across experiments.
insights.roadmapImplication: Evaluate run-to-run alignment as part of the end-to-end LC-MS workflow, including how Waters handles component-level retention shifts without obscuring data provenance or forcing excessive manual review.
insights.watchNext: SCIEX OS release notes, proteomics or small-molecule workflows using the method, prosecution changes, and benchmark evidence for alignment accuracy and processing time.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The assignee is a SCIEX operating-company entity, and the record is a pending application. The filing does not establish that the method is shipping, exclusive, valid, or superior.
